_readme: pk26/D2 — THE SHOP'S MARK, AND IT IS THIS BOX'S OWN APP THAT DRAWS IT. Same format as `seed/chrome.json`
and the same hand (`seed/blocks.mjs`): the mark simply stopped being the platform's business.
★★ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL — the owner's objection, verbatim (08/09): «o app que coloca logo na
vitrine muda o dado em todo lugar, e não só onde tem o bloco dele no compose? … Se não, o compose não faz
sentido, está configurando algo lá que nem sabe onde vai aparecer». He was right, and it was measured:
`chrome/brand` was ONE placement read in FOUR renders — the header bar, the drawer's head, the footer's
brand column and the login modal — so an operator dragged one row and changed four places, and the board
could not say which. pk26/P1 gave each place its own slot; this file is the other half of the answer.
★★ AND IT IS THE DEMONSTRATION ITSELF, which is the second reason it is here and not in the product.
The owner's words: «esse app me ajuda a mostrar para os clientes como eles podem fazer apps livremente
(principal forma de extensão do Forge) … esse mostra mais claramente e de forma simples um logo virando
outro». An app that lives in ONE customer's repository, writes four blocks, ships no page, asks for no
scope and changes the face of four shops is the shortest true answer to «how do I extend Forge?».
⛔ ONE COMPONENT PER PLACE — FOUR, NOT ONE PLACED FOUR TIMES, and this is the KERNEL'S rule rather than a
preference of ours: `placement: 'single'` is enforced per (store, app, component) by `assertSingleFree`
(packages/core/src/commands/composition.ts:176), so the same component in a second slot is refused with
`conflict`. The objection the owner raised was already the contract; it was the `chrome` app that stood
outside it.
★ THE FOUR SLOTS, AND WHAT EACH DRAWS IF NOTHING IS PLACED (pk26/P1's contract):
header_brand   → storefront:header.brand          the shop's top bar                       `forge.`
drawer_brand   → storefront:header.drawer_brand   the mobile drawer's head                 `forge.`
footer_brand   → storefront:footer.brand          the footer's brand column     `forge.` + a tagline
account_brand  → storefront:account.brand         the login box                            `forge.`
★★ THE TAGLINE IS A FIELD, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE FOOTER ENTRY. «Leve. Inteligente. Sua.» is
not new: it is the Forge fallback of `footer.brand`, and that fallback cedes the node as a UNIT — mark AND
sentence together, deliberately, because «the tagline is OUR sentence: leaving it standing under somebody
else's logo would be the same defect one element to the right». So placing a mark in the footer DELETES
the sentence, and the only honest way to keep it is to SAY it. From this file on, the demo's footer says
«Leve. Inteligente. Sua.» because the demo CONFIGURED it — which is a better thing to show a customer than
a shop that inherited somebody else's line.
⛔ AND ONLY THE TWO SHOE SHOPS SAY IT (owner, 08/09: «na loja de sapatos e do outlet»). The café has a
footer of its own and he did not name it; the counter has no shop window at all.
★ THE THREE MARKS ARE THE ONES THE BOX ALREADY WORE — carried over from `seed/chrome.json`'s `brand`
block, byte for byte, so this file changes WHERE the mark is configured and never WHAT it says:
forge  → forge + .store     outlet → forge + .outlet     cafe → the logo file, described `forge.co`
⚠️ TEXT IN THE TWO SHOE SHOPS AND A PICTURE IN THE CAFÉ, and that split is a measurement rather than a
taste. `tail` is drawn in `var(--color-accent)`, one of the six tokens a theme redefines, so a WORD mark
re-tints itself when the theme moves (copper on the reference, carmine on the outlet) and a raster does
not. The café is the one store whose mark this repository actually HAS as art
(`seed/photos/forge-co-logo.png`, the cut the owner delivered — see `bin/chrome-logo-crop.guard.mjs`), and
its forked vitrine bundles the same drawing. In every block the two are EXCLUSIVE: a logo replaces the
words, and `text` becomes the picture's accessible name.
⚠️ THE CAFÉ IS DRESSED IN ALL FOUR ANYWAY, AND THE REASON IS NOT SYMMETRY. Its vitrine is a FORK with its
own chrome (`storefront-coffee/src/components/coffee/CoffeeChrome.tsx` bundles the mark as an import, and
`header.brand` appears NOWHERE in that tree — measured), so `header_brand` and `drawer_brand` draw nothing
there. But the ACCOUNT screens are OURS for every store: `apps/checkout/src/app/s/[store]/(account)/
layout.tsx` mounts the kit's own `StorefrontChrome`, which is where `header.brand` and `footer.brand` are
declared. So the café's four placements render on the screens the café's buyers reach through us — which
is the exact defect the `chrome` app was written for: «our wordmark, in somebody else's shop».
⛔ AND THE COUNTER GETS NOTHING, NAMED RATHER THAN SILENTLY SKIPPED — the same rule `seed/chrome.json`
writes for the same store, and for a stronger reason here: the totem is a whole-host app of its own
(caddy `:82`, no store in the URL) that mounts neither the kit's chrome nor our account screens. Four
placements there would be four rows an operator can drag and never see the effect of.

forge._why: The reference shoe store, on the vanilla storefront image — which is what makes it the honest demonstration: no fork, no theme fork, one app placed four times and the shop is its own. The mark is TEXT (`forge` + `.store`, the tail in the theme's copper accent) and it is the same mark `seed/chrome.json` puts in the funnel's two bars as a PICTURE. ★ The footer says the sentence out loud: until pk26 it inherited «Leve. Inteligente. Sua.» from the Forge fallback, and a placed mark would have deleted it.

outlet._why: The same brand under its own theme, and the mark is where that stops being a claim: `tail` is drawn in the theme's accent — carmine here, copper on the reference — so the SAME four configs make the outlet look like the outlet without a line of code. ⚠️ THE TAIL IS `.outlet`, WITH A POINT, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: it used to be `" Outlet"` and the header read `ForgeOutlet`, glued, because every configured word is trimmed before it is drawn and the two halves are concatenated with nothing between them. The separator has to be a printable CHARACTER. ★ The tagline is the owner's second shop for it (08/09).

cafe._why: ★ THE STORE THE WHOLE ITEM WAS REALLY ABOUT. Its vitrine is a FORK and wears its own chrome; its checkout and its ACCOUNT screens are ours, hosted, and without these placements the café's buyers reach the login box under the REFERENCE wordmark — somebody else's mark in their shop. It is the one entry with a LOGO because it is the one store whose mark this repository has as art: `seed/photos/forge-co-logo.png`, the cut the owner delivered (898x273, 84.6% ink — `bin/chrome-logo-crop.guard.mjs` grades it by proportion, never by filename), the same drawing the fork bundles. `text` is NOT decoration beside it: the picture wins, and the word becomes its accessible name — a logo IS the store's name to a screen reader. ⛔ NO TAGLINE: the owner named the two shoe shops and this one has a footer of its own.
